records.headline: Special weather statement
records.description:
Winter weather travel statement in effect.

What:
Localized snowfall amounts up to 5 cm.
Reduced visibility in areas of heavier snow.

When:
This morning.

Where:
Areas of higher terrain south of Georgian Bay.

Discussion:
Although snowfall amounts are not expected to be overly significant, impacts may be higher than normal as this will be the first snowfall of the season for portions of the region.

Motorists should expect hazardous winter driving conditions and adjust travel plans accordingly.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. Slow down driving in slippery conditions. Watch for taillights ahead and maintain a safe following distance.

For road conditions and other traveller information from the Ministry of Transportation, visit https://www.ontario.ca/511, https://x.com/511Ontario, or call 5-1-1.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

records.area: Greater Victoria Coastline: Cordova Bay to East Sooke
records.headline: Coastal flooding statement
records.description:
This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels are expected with enhanced wave activity and strong winds at times.
 
Hazard: Possible coastal flooding due to storm surge. Water levels will likely exceed highest astronomical tide.
 
When: Today and Sunday. Peak water levels will be observed during high tide, occuring from 11am to 2PM local time.
 
Where:  Low-lying and exposed coastal sections of the Southern Gulf Islands, Saanich Inlet, Swartz Bay to Cordova Bay, Cordova Bay to East Sooke
 
Discussion:
A series of Pacific low-pressure systems are moving across the region and coinciding with a period of high tides this weekend. The storm surge enhancement to the high tide cycle will cause water levels to exceed high astronomical tide.  East to southeasterly winds gusting from 60 to 90 km/h this weekend are expected over exposed coastal sections at times and will cause enhanced wave action and swells in some areas.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

Dense fog has developed over portions of southwestern Saskatchewan.

Conditions will improve later this morning.

Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Fog advisories are issued when widespread poor visibility in fog is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #SKStorm.

Areas of dense fog are expected or occurring.

Conditions are expected to improve later today.

Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Be prepared for areas of near-zero visibility and allow extra time to reach your destination. If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ABstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #ABStorm.

records.headline: Wind warning
records.description:
Damaging winds are expected.

Another strong wind event is expected over coastal B.C.

What: Southeasterly winds of 90 km/h gusting to 110 km/h.

When: Late tonight into Sunday.

Where: Coastal sections of West Vancouver Island, North Vancouver Island, and Haida Gwaii.

Remarks:  Very strong, gusty winds will develop over the BC Coast this evening.  Winds will remain strong overnight and diminish before morning on Vancouver Island, while Haida Gwaii will see a second push of strong winds midday on Sunday.

Local utility outages are possible. Disruptions to services and travel are possible.

Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

records.headline: Rainfall warning
records.description:
Heavy rain is expected.

Another round of significant rain for the west coast. 

When: This afternoon through Sunday night.

Where: Howe Sound and Sea-to-Sky region.

Remarks:
Another moisture laden low pressure system is heading towards the BC coast. Heavy rain is expected to begin late this afternoon and continue through Sunday.  Total amounts of 40 to 70 mm are possible.

Already saturated ground from a series of storms earlier in the week will lessen the soils ability to absorb moisture, which could intensify the impacts of this round of heavy rain.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

records.headline: Blizzard warning
records.description:
Prolonged blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility in blowing snow are expected.

What:
Near-zero visibility in blizzard conditions.

When:
Now through Monday night.

Where:
Dempster Highway near the Richardson Mountains.

Additional information:
A persistent ridge of high pressure over the Beaufort Sea and a low pressure system over the Gulf of Alaska are generating a strong pressure gradient across the Richardson Mountains until Monday night.

Easterly winds of 60 km/h gusting to 80 will further increase to 80 km/h gusting to 110 this morning. Wind-swept snow and falling snow combined with the strong winds will result in blizzard conditions with near-zero visibility. Winds will subside through Sunday, then will strengthen again on Monday. Blizzard conditions will remain.

Road closures are possible.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to YTstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #YTStorm.

records.headline: Flood Warning issued November 14 at 10:14AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
records.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast this weekend into next week due to a combination
of northerly winds, downstream tidal effects, and water from upstream
heavy rainfall working north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EST Saturday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.4 feet just after
midnight tonight. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 1130 AM EST.

records.headline: Flood Warning issued November 14 at 8:03AM MST until November 14 at 9:45AM MST by NWS Salt Lake City UT
records.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...West Central Kane County in southern Utah...
Southeastern Washington County in southwestern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 945 AM MST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of normally dry washes, slot canyons, rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is
occurring. National Park officials reported all area washes and
streams are running high and fast. The river gauge on the North
Fork of the Virgin River continues to increase, currently near 1000
cfs.  Similarly river gauges on the main stem of the Virgin River
upstream of Quail Creek show flows increasing rapidly.  Gould Wash
in Hurricane is running high.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 802 AM MST, local law enforcement reported an area of very
heavy rainfall across the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Zion National Park, Hurricane, La Verkin, Apple Valley,
Toquerville, Leeds, Virgin, Springdale, Rockville and Pintura.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

records.headline: Flood Warning issued November 14 at 8:54AM CST until November 17 at 1:00AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
records.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From this evening to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM CST Saturday the stage was 12.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this evening to a crest of 15.0 feet early tomorrow afternoon. It
will then fall below flood stage late Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.2
feet on 09/19/1983.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

records.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 14 at 5:50AM AKST until November 15 at 5:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
records.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations
between 2 and 4 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze.
Winds gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Seward.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 5 PM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop tonight and continue into
Sunday before warmer air works in and changes the snow over to
rain. A brief period of freezing rain is possible before
temperatures warm above freezing.
records.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

records.headline: Heat Advisory issued November 14 at 9:51AM AST until November 14 at 5:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
records.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...Puerto Rico and Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.
records.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

records.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 7 feet with sets 8 to 10 feet along west-facing beaches.

expected, particularly along west-facing beaches where surf
will be highest.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 10 AM PST Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday.

isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Adjusted high tides will be near 6.2- 6.5
feet around midday today, which will combine with high surf to
produce minor coastal flooding. Highest surf is expected to
occur late today into early Sunday. Surf begins to subside
Sunday afternoon but will remain elevated into Monday.
records.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

stranded, stay in your vehicle.

records.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 14 at 4:02AM PST until November 14 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
records.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8
to 14 feet, peaking Saturday. Surf may locally reach 15 feet
near Ventura Harbor, where surf will likely be the largest.
Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-
northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry,
especially around the time of high tide, including over beach
parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible.
There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents
can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves
can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and
capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west-
northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into
next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely
peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. Minor to
moderate coastal flooding impacts are possible, especially
when largest surf overlaps with peak high tides. Some of these
impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and
shallow flooding of normally dry beaches and walkways.
records.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

records.area: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
records.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 14 at 4:02AM PST until November 15 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
records.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10
to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf
Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet
with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
moderate to significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-
northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM Friday to 3 AM PST Sunday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal
beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and
jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people
off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
Remain far away from the water's edge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells
will create an extended period of large surf into next week,
with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday
night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant
impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with
widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at
Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.
records.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

records.headline: Flood Watch issued November 14 at 3:11AM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
records.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following
county, Mason.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Three to four inches of rain is forecast for the south slopes of
the Olympics through early Sunday with snow levels of 5500 to
6500 feet. The combination of heavy rain and relatively high snow
levels could push the Skokomish River near Potlatch above flood
stage.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

records.description:
* WHAT...High risk of rip currents. Minor coastal flooding
possible around high tide times late Sunday into Monday morning.

* WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches, including the Matagorda
Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water. Strong winds and elevated seas

normal. There is a risk of minor coastal flooding along the low
lying areas from the Bolivar Peninsula to Surfside around high
tide times late Sunday into Monday.
records.instruction: Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

and life-threatening surf conditions. Stay off of beaches, rocks,
jetties, piers, and other waterside infrastructure.

* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves of 30 up to 40 feet.

* WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Sunday. .

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late
Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late
Sunday through Monday.
records.instruction:

run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.

capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

records.area: San Francisco; Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
records.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 14 at 1:05AM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
records.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at
favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, large
breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls,
inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 4 AM PST Sunday. For the
Coastal Flood Advisory, now through 6 PM PST today.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory today is
specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves
will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent
infrastructure.
records.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

infrastructure.

records.area: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; Central Coast of Oregon; South Washington Coast
records.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 14 at 12:53AM PST until November 14 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
records.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf
conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. For the High Surf
Advisory, large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up
to 23 to 28 feet.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST today. For
the High Surf Advisory, from noon today to 4 AM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe
beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night.
records.instruction:
A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

records.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 14 at 3:41AM EST until November 14 at 4:00PM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
records.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM EST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Flooding will be mainly confined to back
bay areas where water levels remain elevated.
records.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

.MON...E wind 25 kt. Seas 16 ft.
.TUE...E wind 20 kt. Seas 14 ft.
.WED...SE wind 30 kt. Seas 10 ft.

records.area: Point Piedras Blancas to Point Sal westward out to 10 NM; East Santa Barbara Channel from Pt. Conception to Pt. Mugu CA including Santa Cruz Island
records.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued November 13 at 2:53PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
records.description:
A large west to northwesterly swell is expected to produce
breaking waves at the Morro Bay and Ventura Harbor entrances
on Saturday. These conditions have a history of capsizing vessels
of various sizes resulting in serious injury or death, even to
the most experienced mariners. Mariners are urged to stay clear of
these harbor entrances. For more information, contact the local
harbor patrol or coast guard station...and continue to monitor
NOAA Weather Radio for the latest weather information..

records.instruction:
Hazard(s) caused by: single falling trees; objects falling to the ground. 
Recommendations for what to do: 
Secure scaffolding and free-standing objects (e.g. screens and platforms/stages). For example, fasten tents and coverings or, if there is enough time, take them down completely. Watch out for falling objects (e.g. large branches, roof tiles) and seek shelter if possible.
